card.name: Era and unit abbreviations after numbers
card.fires_on: The first letter or piece of an abbreviation right after a number, such as B or A in B.C./A.D./B.P., the a in a.m., or 'per' and 'below' after a quantity. It fits dates and measurements in general web text.

modes.label: Era abbreviations
modes.description: The B or A that starts B.C., A.D. or B.P. right after a year or century.
modes.example: in 535<< A>>.D. Justinian's marriage legislation affirmed

modes.label: Time and altitude abbreviations
modes.description: The a or period in a.m. or a.s.l. after a number.
modes.example: began at 4.30 a<<.>> m., and continued all day

modes.label: Units after a number
modes.description: Words like per or below that complete a measurement phrase after a number.
modes.example: the mercury can plunge quickly to 60 degrees<< below>> zero

card.writes: It favors completions of measurement phrases such as squared, Celsius and Fahrenheit.
card.plain: It marks the spot right after a number where an abbreviation like A.D. or a unit like 'per hour' is about to be completed.
